name: Evaluating Variance in Visual Question Answering Benchmarks
description: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have emerged as powerful tools for visual question answering (VQA), enabling reasoning and contextual understanding across visual and textual modalities. Despite their advancements, the evaluation of MLLMs on VQA benchmarks often relies on point estimates, overlooking the significant variance in performance caused by factors such as stochastic model outputs, training seed sensitivity, and hyperparameter configurations. This paper critically examines these issues by analyzing variance across 14 widely used VQA benchmarks, covering diverse tasks such as visual reasoning, text understanding, and commonsense reasoning. We systematically study the impact of training seed, framework non-determinism, model scale, and extended instruction finetuning on performance variability. typical_sota_score: varies substantially by dataset; roughly 60–95% depending on the VQA benchmark
reputation: This is a meta-evaluation study of VQA benchmarks rather than a single canonical benchmark, so it is mainly used by researchers studying evaluation variance.
notes: Focuses on variance and reliability across multiple VQA benchmarks; scores depend on the underlying benchmark and evaluation protocol, with stochasticity and non-determinism being major concerns.
